views.name: pizza_orders_with_runner_and_pizza
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.order_id AS order_id,
  c.customer_id AS customer_id,
  c.pizza_id AS pizza_id,
  p.pizza_name AS pizza_name,
  c.exclusions AS exclusions,
  c.extras AS extras,
  c.order_time AS order_time,
  r.runner_id AS runner_id,
  r.pickup_time AS pickup_time,
  r.distance AS distance,
  r.duration AS duration,
  r.cancellation AS cancellation
FROM pizza_clean_customer_orders c
LEFT JOIN pizza_names p ON c.pizza_id = p.pizza_id
LEFT JOIN pizza_clean_runner_orders r ON c.order_id = r.order_id
views.description: Denormalized view of cleaned pizza orders joined to runner pickup info and pizza name. Useful for questions about order timing, delivery performance, per-pizza order counts, or joining to toppings/extra detail later. | Use for: orders per pizza or per customer; delivery time and distance analysis; join order attributes to runner performance; filter orders by pizza_name or cancellation status

views.name: pizza_order_extras_aggregated
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  g.order_id AS order_id,
  SUM(COALESCE(g.extras_count,0)) AS total_extras_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT g.extras) AS distinct_extras_count
FROM pizza_get_extras g
GROUP BY g.order_id
views.description: Aggregated counts of extras per order using the detailed pizza_get_extras table. One row per order with total extras and distinct extra-item count. Useful for questions about average extras per order or joining to toppings for popular extras. | Use for: average extras per order; orders with many extras; joining extras aggregates back to orders/customers

views.name: pizza_order_exclusions_aggregated
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.order_id AS order_id,
  SUM(COALESCE(e.total_exclusions,0)) AS total_exclusions_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT e.exclusions) AS distinct_exclusions_count
FROM pizza_get_exclusions e
GROUP BY e.order_id
views.description: Aggregated counts of exclusions per order using the detailed pizza_get_exclusions table. One row per order with total exclusions (sum of reported totals) and distinct exclusion items. Useful for analyzing customization or special requests. | Use for: orders with many exclusions; customization patterns by customer or pizza; join exclusions to toppings to see which are most removed

views.name: pizza_recipes_exploded
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.pizza_id AS pizza_id,
  TRIM(r.token) AS topping_token,
  CASE
    WHEN TRIM(r.token) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN instr(TRIM(r.token), '.') = 0 AND trim(r.token) GLOB '[0-9]*' THEN CAST(TRIM(r.token) AS INTEGER)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS topping_id
FROM (
  SELECT
    pizza_id,
    -- iterative splitting using recursive-like technique with correlated subqueries limits: build tokens by repeatedly finding next comma
    -- get first token
    CASE
      WHEN instr(toppings, ',') = 0 THEN toppings
      ELSE substr(toppings, 1, instr(toppings, ',') - 1)
    END AS token,
    -- remaining string after first comma (may be '')
    CASE
      WHEN instr(toppings, ',') = 0 THEN ''
      ELSE substr(toppings, instr(toppings, ',') + 1)
    END AS rest
  FROM pizza_recipes
  UNION ALL
  -- subsequent tokens: repeatedly take from rest until empty
  SELECT
    pizza_id,
    CASE
      WHEN instr(rest, ',') = 0 THEN rest
      ELSE substr(rest, 1, instr(rest, ',') - 1)
    END AS token,
    CASE
      WHEN instr(rest, ',') = 0 THEN ''
      ELSE substr(rest, instr(rest, ',') + 1)
    END AS rest
  FROM (
    SELECT
      pizza_id,
      -- second pass: take rest from first pass
      CASE
        WHEN instr(toppings, ',') = 0 THEN ''
        ELSE substr(toppings, instr(toppings, ',') + 1)
      END AS rest,
      toppings,
      pizza_id AS pid
    FROM pizza_recipes
  )
) r
views.description: Exploded mapping of pizza_id to individual topping ids by parsing the comma-separated toppings text in pizza_recipes. One row per pizza_id + topping_id (as integer when parseable). Useful for joining pizzas to pizza_toppings, counting toppings per pizza, and identifying popular toppings by pizza. | Use for: join pizzas to toppings; count toppings per pizza; find pizzas that include a given topping id

views.name: runner_performance_by_runner
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.runner_id AS runner_id,
  COUNT(r.order_id) AS deliveries_count,
  AVG(r.distance) AS avg_distance,
  AVG(r.duration) AS avg_duration,
  SUM(CASE WHEN r.cancellation IS NOT NULL AND trim(r.cancellation) != '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cancellation_count
FROM pizza_clean_runner_orders r
GROUP BY r.runner_id
views.description: Aggregated performance metrics per runner from cleaned runner orders: total deliveries, average distance, average duration, cancellation count. One row per runner_id. Useful for ranking runners or comparing average delivery metrics across runners. | Use for: which runner has fastest average duration; runner workload by number of deliveries; impact of cancellations per runner

views.name: trees_by_zipcode_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.zipcode AS zipcode,
  t.boroname AS boroname,
  COUNT(*) AS tree_count,
  AVG(t.tree_dbh) AS avg_tree_dbh,
  SUM(CASE WHEN t.status IS NOT NULL AND trim(t.status) != '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS status_count
FROM trees t
GROUP BY t.zipcode, t.boroname
views.description: Aggregated tree counts and average tree diameter per zipcode/boroname. One row per zipcode and boroname combination. Useful for neighborhood-level tree analyses and joining to zipcode-level demographic/income tables. | Use for: compare tree density across zipcodes; join tree aggregates to income by zipcode; neighborhood tree health or size summaries

views.name: companies_funding_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.company_id AS company_id,
  COALESCE(f.valuation,0) AS valuation,
  COALESCE(f.funding,0) AS funding,
  f.select_investors AS select_investors
FROM companies_funding f
views.description: Normalized view exposing company funding and valuation with COALESCE safeguards. One row per company_id. Useful as a base for funding analyses, joins to dates/industries, and calculating ratios like funding/valuation. | Use for: funding to valuation ratios; join funding to company founding year or industry; identify companies with missing funding/valuation

views.name: companies_with_dates_and_industries
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.company_id AS company_id,
  d.date_joined AS date_joined,
  d.year_founded AS year_founded,
  i.industry AS industry,
  f.valuation AS valuation,
  f.funding AS funding,
  f.select_investors AS select_investors
FROM companies_funding f
LEFT JOIN companies_dates d ON f.company_id = d.company_id
LEFT JOIN companies_industries i ON f.company_id = i.company_id
views.description: Joined company dimension combining funding, founding year, and industry labels. One row per company_id with available date and industry attributes. Useful for cohort analyses by year_founded or industry and for comparing funding across cohorts. | Use for: funding by year founded or industry; investor analysis by industry; time-based joins for cohorting companies

views.name: covid_statistics_latest_by_state
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.date AS date,
  s.state AS state,
  s.total_cases AS total_cases,
  s.total_deaths AS total_deaths,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY s.state ORDER BY s.date DESC) AS date_rank
FROM statistics s
views.description: Latest statistics row per state based on the date field. Exposes a rank so downstream queries can filter to rank=1 for latest. Useful for state-level current case/death totals and comparisons across states. | Use for: current totals per state (filter where date_rank = 1); time series per state (use date and totals); rank states by latest total_cases or total_deaths

views.name: income_by_zip_normalized
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  i.zipcode AS zipcode,
  COALESCE(i.Estimate_Total,0) AS Estimate_Total,
  COALESCE(i.Margin_of_Error_Total,0) AS Margin_of_Error_Total,
  COALESCE(i.Estimate_Median_income,0) AS Estimate_Median_income,
  COALESCE(i.Margin_of_Error_Median_income,0) AS Margin_of_Error_Median_income,
  COALESCE(i.Estimate_Mean_income,0) AS Estimate_Mean_income,
  COALESCE(i.Margin_of_Error_Mean_income,0) AS Margin_of_Error_Mean_income
FROM income_trees i
views.description: Normalized income estimates per zipcode with COALESCE defaults and clearer column aliases preserved. One row per zipcode. Useful when joining income data to trees or other zipcode-level datasets. | Use for: join income to tree aggregates by zipcode; median or mean income comparisons across zipcodes; filter zipcodes with missing income estimates
